links.comparator_used: Manual physician-written ED discharge notes (session 1) versus physician-edited LLM drafts (session 2)
links.outcome: Note quality (4C Likert scores) and documentation time per note
links.effect: LLM-assisted vs manual: completeness 4.23 vs 4.03, correctness 4.38 vs 4.20, conciseness 4.23 vs 4.11, clinical utility 4.17 vs 3.85 (all P < .001). Median time per note 69.5 s (95% CI, 65.5-78.0) manual vs 32.0 s (95% CI, 29.5-36.0) LLM-assisted (P < .001).
links.tradeoff: Physician editing of the LLM drafts lowered completeness (4.23 vs 4.34; P = .001) and correctness (4.38 vs 4.45; P < .001) relative to the unedited drafts. Clinical utility was equivalent (4.17 vs 4.16).
links.quote: The median documentation time per note dropped from 69.5 (95% CI, 65.5-78.0) seconds for manual notes to 32.0 (95% CI, 29.5-36.0) seconds for LLM-assisted notes (P < .001).

design_hint: clinician review and editing of LLM-drafted notes
